sentences.text: MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 36326 of 2024  AMRAT
Versus  THE STATE OF M.P. AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Anurag Vyas - advocate for the applicant.
Shri Kshitij Vyas, learned Panel Lawyer for the responde  ORDER Heard and perused the record.

2. This is the first application filed by the applicants for grant of regular bail under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 relating to FIR No.10/2024, dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station - Badnawar, District - Dhar for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376,
376(2)(n), 376(3) of IPC, 1860 and Sections 3/4 and 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 14.05.2024.
3. Allegation against the applicant is that of abduction and commission of rape with the prosecutrix.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
As per statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the relationship between the prosecutrix and applicant, seems to be consensual.
It is further submitted that the applicant and prosecutrix have resided with each other for a period of five months.
The applicant is in in custody since 14.05.2024 i.e. almost four months.
Final conclusion of trial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26723 2 MCRC-36326-2024 will take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that the applicant be released on bail.
5. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent - State opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

sentences.text:
6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.
7.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for both the parties, custody period of the applicant and also the fact final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time, I deem it proper to release the accused / applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of

Rs.
50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

The applicant shall abide by all the conditions enumerated u/S. 480(3) of BNSS.
9.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
